title: Orders API: ambiguous, incomplete handover
source: synthetic, written for the end-to-end suite (12 Oct)
proves: A thin KT: a first check that is not a fix, a rollback described only as 'usually quick', a risky migration, no owners, a half-remembered environment, and one speech-recognition error ('Argo City' for ArgoCD) whose intended term is unambiguous in context.
transcript: Right, so this is a quick handover for the orders API, which serves order history to the mobile app. It's a small API running on Kubernetes, and it uses PostgreSQL and Redis. GitHub Actions builds the images and Argo City deploys them. Grafana shows the service health. A couple of months ago we had an incident where the database ran out of connections. If you see that again, check the pool metrics first. Rolling back is usually quick. One warning: the last database migration might be hard to reverse, so be careful with it. Um, there's a staging cluster too, but I can't remember what's different about it. I think that's most of it.
